newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: IPCO signs deal with Malaysian state.
newsitem.headline: IPCO signs deal with Malaysian state.

text.p: The IPCO group said on Sunday its Malaysian subsidiary has signed an agreement with the Malaysian state government of Perlis to conduct studies on a water supply system.

The agreement grants IPCO Constructors Sdn Bhd exclusive rights to conduct the detailed study, after which the company is expected to submit a proposal to develop the 12 million gallons per day water supply system, an IPCO statement said.
IPCO submitted a proposal to the Perlis government last year, saying the state would need substantial new sources of treated water in light of several planned large development projects in the area.
IPCO is currently constructing a similar treated water system in Malaysia's northern Langkawi island.
The Singapore-based group develops, contracts, and invests in infrastructure projects around the world.
It gave no financial details on the agreement, but said the water supply project is not expected to contribute to turnover and profit in the current financial year ending June 30, 1997.
